title: What If a La Palma Landslide Sent a Tsunami Across the Atlantic?

scenes.text: What if half a volcano slid into the sea? The famous tsunami warning may be wrong.
The idea started with a 2001 paper on La Palma in the Canary Islands, using a slide of 500 cubic kilometers.
That model predicted waves of 20 to 25 meters on the Florida coast.
A later simulation of a slide of 375 cubic kilometers found waves two to three times lower in Florida.
The same worst case still hits the Canaries hard. Some islands would see waves of dozens of meters, up to 188 at El Hierro.
Researchers say such collapses happen in steps, not one slide. Deposits of a giant wave have never been found in the Americas.

description:
What if a huge piece of La Palma slid into the Atlantic?
The famous 25 meter wave for the US coast was an extreme guess, and later models found it would be two to three times lower.
